records.type: The convoy consisted of one large AK or AP, five medium AK's
records.title: Attack 1 · The convoy consisted of one large AK or AP, five

fields.description: The convoy consisted of one large AK or AP, five medium AK's or AP's, and three escorts (one a two stack destroy- er, one ⟦CH⟧ or PC, and the other not seen). The contact was made by sighting smoke and later seeing tops of the targets. After dark six shapes were counted at about 7000 yards. The escorts could not be seen until about 5000 yards. The large AK or AP was definitely seen as a modern ship of from 8-10,000 tons. The only other target definitely silhouetted by an explosion was an old M-F-M freighter of about 5000 tons. The near es- cort was long, low and had two stacks. He was seen at 900 yards. The PC was identified as such by his smaller relative size.
fields.attack_type: Surface radar attack, using T.B.T. bearings for firing 1st torpedo and generated bearings for 2nd and 3rd tor- pedo. Range was excessive due to position of escort. Overlapping targets presented unusually good target. Escort not fired on as did not want to take time to set torpedoes to shallow depth. Assumed target length of 400 feet and used 100% spread coverage.

fields.narrative: At with destroyer bearing 005º relative, range 1100 yards, fired three torpedo spread at leading ship of the near column using a 327º gyro angle, 112º(P) track, and 3750 yard range. With destroyer dead ahead, fired a three torpedo spread at three overlapping ships which were next astern using a 350º gyro angle, 90º(P) track, and 3500 yard range. These torpedoes passed under the bow of the destroyer who was frantically signalling and had stopped. Due to the proximity of the escort, his movements were followed more closely than those of the targets after we fired. The following facts were definitely noted: (1) Explosions were seen from the bridge on two targets; (2) Five torpedo explosions were heard topside and below; (3) The soundman reported five torpedo explosions; (4) The times of the explosions checked well with expected torpedo runs; (5) One of the ships in the second target group was stopped and completely covered with greyish smoke similar to ships sunk on other patrols by this ship; (6) Neither of the observed explosions was on the smoking ship; and (7) No depth charges were seen or heard until after the last torpedo explosion. Entering the field of deduction, the torpedo runs indicated a hit on the first ship, a hit on a ship in the far column, two hits on a near ship in the overlapping group of three, and a hit on a ship in the far column. It is believed the ship covered with smoke received two hits and probably sunk. As the radar was kept on the escort during the evasion, no information relative to the targets was obtained.

fields.narrative: At swung ship 180º, set after tubes on 4 feet, and drew a bead on the destroyer. Intended to let him have a salvo in order to dampen his ardor. He turned toward us blinked a red light and we fired three torpedoes down the throat at 1100 yards. He jogged left and evaded. No hits. Saw the destroyer drop one depth charge. Escorts around the targets dropped several depth charges. The destroyer let us open to 2500 yards before using his gun. He apparently was not sure we were not another escort until we fired at him. The gunfire fell 500 yards wide. Another escort headed in our direction, but dropped behind as we speeded up. At 3400 yards range the destroyer decided it was safe to follow us and he held the range steady. Four main engines would not get us clear. At this point a nearly full moon cleared the clouds and the destroyer became more accurate with his gunfire.

               Details of Action
Conducted battle surface, closed range on surface from 4000 to
2100 yards, and opened fire on last sampan in column of six headed for
Nomwin Island, with 4" gun, three 20 MM machine guns, and 2 air cooled
50 caliber machine guns. The 4" gun fire was not as effective as us-
ual due to smallness of target, the targets movements, and the stiff-
ness of the foot firing device. The gun captain fired the gun on
pointer's "Fire". Stiffness of foot firing device was due to bending
of linkage in rough seas. The target was straddled continually. The
range varied between 2000 yards and 900 yards. Some shells of common
ammunition seemed to pass thru the target without exploding. About
ten 4" hits were observed in addition to those hits not exploding.
Broke off action with only 18 rounds of 4" ammunition left, and after
wrecking sampan experienced jams with all three 20 MM guns. These
jams were as follows: #1 20 MM broken firing pin; #2 20 MM defec-
tive ammunition; and #3 20 MM broken firing pin.
Fired Following Ammunition:
    42 rounds    4" H.C. (sensitive nose)
    30 rounds    4" Common
  1026 rounds    20 MM
  1110 rounds    50 Caliber

       tower on Oroluk Island. No separate report made as no positive re-

fields.narrative: Surfaced, closed range from 4000 to 2100 yards on last sampan and opened fire. The five leading sampans continued with best speed toward the pass, and the last sampan, in spite of 4" hits and small arms fire, tried to close range to us to make his machine gun more effective. He forced us to continually turn away to stay out of effective machine gun range. We straddled him continually, but obtained only about ten 4" hits with 72 rounds. These hits left the target's hull holed, topside demolished, engine exploded, and all personnel killed that didn't jump overboard. The target was left floating. Cleared area before Truk should send a plane after us since other sampans had reached pass in Hall Atoll. As we had closed Nomwin Island to with 2 1/2 miles and not received any gunfire, it is assumed no sizable guns are located there.
